title: Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa
hook: on the climb to Sabarimala, every stranger on the path is called swami

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa: the impossible cure, and the boy who came home riding a tigress. Today, the last of the Kerala days.

Swami. A man in a black dhoti says it to the tea seller at the bottom of the hill. The tea seller says it back. A pilgrim with gray hair says it to a teenager who's stopped to catch his breath, and the teenager says it to him. On the forest path up to Sabarimala, it's how people greet each other, thank each other, ask each other to move aside. Swami: the word for a master, a holy one, the Lord, used for everyone. Today, the pilgrimage up Ayyappa's hill.
screen: `SWAMI, SAID TO EVERYONE` → `A FOREST PATH UP A HILL` → `THE NAME EVERY PILGRIM SHARES`

segments.voice: Tradition says that when Manikandan's work on earth was done, he shot an arrow and asked that his temple be built where it fell. It fell on a hill in the forest: Sabarimala, where Ayyappa is worshiped seated in meditation. Pilgrims don't just set out. For a season before the climb they keep a vow. They wear a bead necklace, dress in black or dark blue, eat simple food, give up alcohol and keep celibacy, and often walk barefoot. From the day the necklace goes on, the pilgrim is called swami, and even Ayyappa, by name. The vow makes the pilgrim a little like the god they're going to see. Each pilgrim climbs with the irumudi on the head, a cloth bundle tied in two parts. One part carries offerings, including a coconut filled with ghee for the god. The other carries food for the road. The forest echoes with a chant: Swamiye saranam Ayyappa, Lord, you are my refuge, Ayyappa. On the way, pilgrims stop at Erumeli, where Ayyappa's companion in the stories, a Muslim named Vavar, is honored too. Rich and poor, old and young, wear the same dark cloth, carry the same bundle, and answer to the same name. Tradition says that above the shrine are the words tat tvam asi, that thou art, from the Upanishads. Some hear it as the god speaking to the pilgrim: what you came looking for, you are.
screen: `WHERE THE ARROW FELL` · `A SEASON OF VOWS` · `THE IRUMUDI ON THE HEAD` · `THAT THOU ART`

segments.voice: Breathe in slowly, and on each out-breath take one step up a forest hill in your mind. Each time a face comes to mind, someone easy or someone hard, greet them inwardly the pilgrim's way: swami. If you pray, you can say the pilgrims' chant, Swamiye saranam Ayyappa, softly, in time with the steps.
Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa. Today, the pilgrimage to Sabarimala: the vow, the two-part bundle, the chant, and every pilgrim called swami. Today's word.
Your line: Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa. A king welcomed home with flowers, and a hill where every stranger is swami. Kerala, complete.

chat.says: Why do Sabarimala pilgrims call everyone, even strangers, swami?
options: From the day the bead necklace goes on, each pilgrim is called swami, even Ayyappa.
It's a polite word for an elder, so only the older pilgrims are meant by it.
It's a title for priests, and pilgrims use it when asking them for blessings.
chat.meaning: On the vow, every pilgrim is called swami and even Ayyappa; rich and poor wear the same cloth and answer to the same name.
